messages:
maria: Quick follow-up to the operator auth RFC — I sketched some edgecases where operator svc + project-scoped API keys cause ambiguous origin.

alex: can you paste a quick example?

maria: sure. imagine operator-bridge makes calls into payment-svc on behalf of project:123. If it uses a project API key owned by org:acme the runtime sees org claim + service principal. who gets billed / rate-limited? who gets audit events?

sam: hmm. currently we map api_key -> project for routing, and token -> operator for actor. this collision happens when operator proxies a project key.

jordan: possibilities:
- disallow proxying long-lived project keys (prefer ephemeral operator tokens)
- attach origin claim to proxied requests: "x-origin-service: operator-bridge", "x-origin-project: project:123"
- runtime enforces attribution rules: prefer origin claim for billing + rate limits, but keep project tag for data scoping

maria: +1 on origin claim. but we need a fallback for older clients that can't set headers.

alex: fallback idea: issuer of API key vs immediate caller. If the immediate caller is a different service principal than api_key owner, mark as "proxied" and treat quotas as combined with operator's bucket unless project explicitly requested deduction. Not ideal.

security-bot: security-checklist: ensure token exchange path emits audit events with both subject and actor. store both in event blob.

sam: migration plan suggestion:
1) telemetry: emit a flag when proxied keys observed (2w)
2) enforce origin-claim on new operator releases (4w)
3) runtime policy: if origin-claim missing and proxied detected, apply soft-fallback (warn + no billing change) for 30d
4) hard-enforce: deny proxied access or require token exchange (60d)

maria: ops questions — how does rate-limit counting work? we have per-project and per-service quotas.

devops-bot: from infra: rate-limiter supports multiplexed keys: it takes a primary key id and optional secondary tags. We can add flag to prefer actor when proxied.

alex: implementation sketch:
```
// request metadata
{ api_key_id: "ak_123", caller_principal: "svc.operator-bridge", origin_claim: "project:123" }

// decision
if (origin_claim) { attribution = origin_claim; } else if (caller_principal != api_key_owner) { attribution = caller_principal_with_proxied_flag; }
```

jordan: also consider RBAC: proxied calls should not implicitly grant extra privileges. operator should only be able to request subsets of project permissions.

maria: agreed. next steps: I'll open a tiny RFC to add (1) origin claim header standard, (2) telemetry flags, (3) runtime policy soft-fallback timeline. @alex @sam can you own the runtime + limiter changes? @jordan can you own RBAC constrains + audit schema?

alex: happy to

sam: yep

jordan: on it

maria: cool — logging note: make sure audit entries include both api_key_id and proxied_by so incidents can trace.

security-bot: filing ticket: SEC-8245 generated for audit schema change

maria: thanks all. will sync in the RFC doc, ping me if blockers pop up :handshake:
